subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

I asked my friend to ___________________ against her employers who are doing wrong to her.
solution:
The correct answer is: **fight fire with fire.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"fight fire with fire"** means to respond to an attack or a problem with similar tactics or methods. (आग का जवाब आग से देना)

 
 
• **Example: **When the competitor launched a negative ad campaign, the company decided to **fight fire with fire** and released their own series of aggressive ads.
 
 
 
• The idiom "fight fire with fire" fits in the context of the given sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

**Complete Sentence**:* I asked my friend to fight fire with fire__ against her employers who are doing wrong to her.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Fine words butter no parsnips** (अच्छे शब्द पेट नहीं भरते): This idiom means that fine words or promises do not accomplish anything useful.

 
 
• **Example:** He promised a lot during his campaign, but fine words butter no parsnips; we need action.
 
 
 
• **Finders keepers, losers weepers** (जो पाता है वही रखता है, जो खोता है वही रोता है): This idiom means that the person who finds something can keep it, and the person who lost it has no right to it.
 
 
• **Example: **When I found the money on the street, I kept it because finders keepers, losers weepers.
 
 
 
• **Fight the good fight** (अच्छे कारण के लिए संघर्ष करना): To make a strenuous effort in the face of adversity, often for a noble cause.
 
 
• **Example:** She decided to fight the good fight and stood up for the rights of the underprivileged.
